subject: Benchmarking checkpoint & handoff: HelioHealth onboard
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <alex@heliohealth.com>, Tina Choi <tina.choi@heliohealth.com>
Cc: procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Benchmarking kickoff & proposed test matrix

Alex / Tina —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As promised, attaching our proposed benchmark matrix to make the first pass explicit so CS/Eng can align on targets and artifacts we’ll need to hand over. High-level plan is below and I’ve looped in Monica and Dev from CS/Eng to pick up technical coordination.

Proposed quick agenda for the kickoff call (30m):
- Confirm acceptance criteria (p50/p95/p99 targets, tokenization differences)
- Agree on load test windows and test harness access
- Identify required artifacts (sample prompts, warmup traces, API keys for staging)
- Schedule result review and sign-off cadence

Key assumptions in the attached matrix:
- Target steady-state throughput: 1200 requests/min across 4 concurrent clients
- P50 latency goal (text generation, seq len ~256): <= 120ms
- P99 latency goal: <= 700ms
- Failure budget: 0.5% non-2xx during test window

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-matrix.csv (CSV stub)

Next step: Monica to propose exact runbook and Dev to confirm whether any network whitelists are required. I’ll set a 30m kickoff for early next week unless you prefer otherwise.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: Alex Morton <alex@heliohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff & proposed test matrix

Jonas —

Thanks, this looks good. A couple of clarifying items before we lock the kickoff slot: 
- The 1200 rpm steady-state target looks roughly right for our projected peak. Can you confirm expected token rates per request? Our payloads average ~350 tokens output.
- We will need a one-hour maintenance window in our staging VPC to allow your test traffic. Procurement will coordinate access once SOW milestone #1 is signed — I’ve copied them here.

Prefer next Tuesday (2026-12-15) 10:00am PT for the kickoff call. If that works, please send a calendar invite and brief runbook.

—Alex
Alex Morton
Head of ML, HelioHealth
alex@heliohealth.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morton <alex@heliohealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff & proposed test matrix

Alex / team —

Thanks — following up with the concrete runbook and the acceptance gating logic we’ll use. Attaching the test-harness-config.yaml and a condensed checklist below.

Planned test windows (staging):
- Smoke: 10m at low RPS to validate credentials and warm caches
- Ramp: 15m ramp from 10% -> 100% of target RPS
- Steady: 30m steady at 1200 rpm (20 rps aggregate)
- Spike: 5 x short 1m bursts at 150% to validate throttles/fallbacks

Acceptance metrics (applied to steady window):
- p50 <= 120ms (text generation, 256 token target)
- p95 <= 320ms
- p99 <= 700ms
- Error rate <= 0.5% (2xx expected)
- Median tokens/response ~350 (we’ll also provide distribution)

Artifacts we’ll push to your Drive folder once we start:
- Continuous traces (zip)
- Per-route latency histograms (CSV)
- Request/response samples (redacted PHI)

Notes on data handling: all collected artifacts are scoped to staging, will be redacted for PHI and retained per the SOW (30 days). If you need a longer retention window for analysis, let us know and we can adjust.

Attachments: test-harness-config.yaml (stub)

I’ll be on the kickoff and will take point on the test execution. Dev, Marcus — can you confirm any special network config needed?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Alex Morton <alex@heliohealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff & proposed test matrix

Looping in technical specifics —

We do not expect any persistent changes to your staging environment. For the smoke and ramp runs we’ll need the following:
- A short-lived API key scoped to the staging model endpoint (expires after test window)
- Optional: whitelist Redwood runner egress CIDRs (I’ll drop exact CIDRs in the kickoff meeting)
- TLS cert verification enabled (we test against your staging endpoint host)

Test harness notes:
- We will use our open-source runner (artifacts attached) which simulates KV cache warmup and realistic inter-request intervals.
- We will generate warmup traces that will prime the model K-V cache for the steady window; these are replay-only and do not count toward acceptance tokens.

Attachment references: redwood-benchmark-runner (we uploaded to the shared Drive).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Alex Morton <alex@heliohealth.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff & proposed test matrix

Monica / Dev —

This is great — confirmed on our side: we’ll prepare a short-lived staging API key and create the Drive folder you referenced. Procurement is preparing the access form (should be with you by EOD tomorrow).

I also attached our formal acceptance criteria PDF to make sure legal and procurement are aligned. Two operational asks:
1) Can you publish a short post-test artifact (one-pager) that highlights the pass/fail decisions and where regression tolerances live? We prefer a single artifact to attach to our internal sprint review.
2) We’d like the results review call to include a short demo of the traces to show how warmup impacted tail latency.

Thanks — I’ll accept the Tue 12/15 10:00am PT invite once I see it.

—Alex
(attachment: helio-acceptance-criteria.pdf)
